description: kron-native — the kron entry on Kotlin/Native: edixoi on kron, the Kotlin port of the ioxide io_uring runtime, on its raw recv/send API and nothing above it, as one native binary with no JVM (the Dockerfile's KRON_RUNTIME build arg, set to native); the kron entry runs the same code, at the same kron commit, on the JVM. One reactor per core, each owning its ring and its share of the SO_REUSEPORT listeners; multishot accept and recv into provided buffer rings, the ring driven by hand from Kotlin over the kernel's own io_uring header through cinterop (no liburing). Handlers are Kotlin suspend functions that the reactor resumes inline on the thread that took the completion, with no dispatcher and no thread pool. The HTTP/1.1 handling (request line, query string, case-insensitive headers, Content-Length and chunked bodies, keep-alive, pipelining, reads fragmented across recv boundaries) is edixoi's, ported to Kotlin — no framework, no router. One handler answers on both doors: plaintext on :8080, and TLS on :8081 for json-tls and the 8gbit echo, terminated with BoringSSL linked into the binary, with kernel TX offload where the kernel has the tls module and BoringSSL receive. The async profile's wait is an IORING_OP_TIMEOUT on the reactor's ring, so a held connection costs a kernel deadline rather than a thread. Companion to kron (the same code on the JVM), edixoi (C#) and edixoi-kt, which serve the same profiles.
